trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Check whether any Reuters/AP/official Israeli or Syrian government wire corroborates the market move; confirm EIS premarket/intraday reaction and volume.
time_plan.1h: Compare EIS move versus broad EM and US equity beta to isolate idiosyncratic Israel component.
time_plan.2h: Scan for official denials or walk-backs from Damascus/Jerusalem that would reverse the probability shift.
time_plan.6h: Reassess whether the move persists into the US session and whether Israeli single names (banks, defense) confirm direction.
time_plan.12h: Mark final EIS return; judge whether signal was leak-driven or noise and whether threshold was reached.

predictions.reasoning: A sharp jump in the implied probability of Syria normalizing with Israel would signal broader Middle East de-escalation and regional diplomatic momentum, which is a modest positive for Israeli risk assets. EIS is the most liquid broad proxy for Israeli equity. However, Syria-Israel normalization is a deep long-tail outcome and any single diplomacy signal rarely moves a diversified equity ETF by more than a few percent in 12 hours.

trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Confirm whether oil is actually reacting or moving on unrelated supply/demand news.
time_plan.1h: Check Brent-WTI spread and whether any regional supply headlines dominate.
time_plan.2h: Assess if broader MENA de-escalation narrative is building across wires.
time_plan.6h: Re-evaluate oil move against DXY and risk sentiment to isolate geopolitics.
time_plan.12h: Record final USO return and note low signal-to-noise for this mapping.

predictions.reasoning: Regional de-escalation implied by Syria-Israel normalization could trim the Middle East geopolitical risk premium in oil. But Syria is a negligible producer and the risk-premium channel is diffuse and dominated by OPEC, inventories, and demand; the proxy exposure is weak and direction can easily reverse.

evidence_used: Market question on Syria joining Abraham Accords, resolution requiring a formal publicly-acknowledged Israel-Syria normalization by end-2026
Liquidity-based choice of EIS as Israel equity proxy and USO as oil geopolitical-premium proxy
uncertainty_notes: Syria normalization is a deep tail event; even a sharp probability move may reflect speculation not leaked fact
Equity and commodity proxies have weak, diffuse exposure to this specific diplomatic event
12h window is short relative to how slowly diplomacy news is priced into broad ETFs
The 700bps tradable threshold is very unlikely to be met by either proxy

llm_justification.summary: A sharp upward move in the implied probability of Syria joining the Abraham Accords would signal Middle East de-escalation, modestly supporting Israeli equities (EIS up) and modestly pressuring the oil geopolitical risk premium (USO down). Both mappings are weak: the proxies are diversified and dominated by unrelated drivers, and Syria is both a tail diplomatic case and a negligible oil producer. Expected moves are well below the 700bps tradable threshold, so this is a low-confidence, non-tradable research signal.
key_assumptions: A probability spike reflects genuine de-escalation information rather than pure speculation
De-escalation is net positive for Israeli equities and net negative for oil risk premium
No dominant unrelated macro driver overwhelms the signal in the 12h window
failure_modes: The probability move reverses on official denials, making proxy moves noise
The development may already be public/priced, so no incremental asset move
EIS and USO have weak exposure to Syria specifically; moves driven by US/EM beta or OPEC/inventory news
Normalization could be read as regional realignment that raises, not lowers, tensions, flipping the sign
Magnitude far below 700bps threshold renders the mapping non-tradable
llm_justification.why_not_ex_post: The card is timestamped, content-hashed, and never overwritten. Execution must reject any card created after an anomaly's trigger time.
